keySentence: Jim survived not by strength alone but by quick thinking.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Thinking before acting is wise. Jim understood even his enemies. Your brain is your greatest treasure! Jim survived not by strength alone but by quick thinking.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Jim learned that staying calm helps you think better. Understanding your opponent gives you an advantage. Jim even tried to understand Silver's point of view. This made Jim a better strategist and problem solver. Jim survived not by strength alone but by quick thinking. Practicing thinking skills is something everyone can do every day.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Looking back on his adventure, Jim realized that his greatest strength was his ability to think clearly. Every challenge he overcame was solved through careful analysis rather than physical force. He learned to control his emotions and examine situations from multiple perspectives. Even understanding Silver's motivations helped Jim make smarter decisions. Jim survived not by strength alone but by quick thinking. However, developing strong thinking skills does not happen overnight. Because Jim was naturally curious and always asked questions, his mind grew sharper over time. The most important treasure Jim discovered was not gold but the incredible power of the human mind.
